reuse.why: No shared selection of month-wide categories is introduced or reused; the new action copies the set3MonthAvg skeleton and each action keeps its own SQL query, fixed-id lookup and income check (only NO_SAVED_TEMPLATES and getFixedCategoryIds are shared).

duplication.why: The category SELECT with the includeHiddenCategories interpolation, the getFixedCategoryIds skip and the income/tracking check are pasted into setZero, setLastMonthSpending, set3MonthAvg, set6MonthAvg and set12MonthAvg, and copyPreviousMonth has a sixth variant.

placement.why: Everything stays in budget/actions.ts and the handler is registered next to the other budget methods in budget/app.ts, as the tree does.

scope.why: Edits stay within month-wide actions and the new handler; the TRIM/case-insensitive tweaks are small extras.

maintainability.why: Every exclusion rule over the four steps had to be added in five or six places, and the next rule will too; the skip rule is split between SQL, a JS id set and per-row checks.

bypasses_abstraction.where: budget/actions.ts: setZero, setLastMonthSpending, set3/6/12MonthAvg and copyPreviousMonth each build their own category selection rather than one month-wide selection helper.

disguised_duplication.where: copyPreviousMonth expresses the template and fixed exclusions as a templatedIds set plus row checks, while the other actions express them as SQL plus fixedIds checks: the same rule in a reshaped form.

abstraction_drift.where: No shared selection function exists; all six month-wide actions (copyPreviousMonth, setZero, setLastMonthSpending, set3MonthAvg, set6MonthAvg, set12MonthAvg) re-implement the hidden, template, #fixed and income rules locally, each gaining its own includeHiddenCategories branch.
